findings.reason: the section should name `_refuse_duplicate_id` as the owning mechanism and retire the parallel sprint check, so a caller meets one duplicate-id policy rather than two.
findings.text: §7 lands the append-path duplicate-id refusal through the shared `_refuse_duplicate_id` (reckon/_store.py:2373), but its own text names `create_sprint`'s hand-rolled check `any(isinstance(s, dict) and s.get("id") == sprint_id for s in sprints)` (reckon/mcp.py:2927) only as precedent and leaves it in place, so the codebase ships two implementations of one duplicate-id refusal that differ in shape (an `OpError` with `existing_item` versus an inline `{ok: false, error: ...}` dict)

findings.reason: on the supplied figures (public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23) a pure addition to the tool surface must say in its own text why the single-pair form cannot be folded into the batch path, or what it replaces.
findings.text: §10 adds a `replacements` parameter to the `edit_plan` text surface and a new public `replace_plan_text_batch`, and its own text states the single-pair form is retained ("The single-pair form behaves as it does today"), naming no surface it retires, merges, or cannot retire

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the write path hides the lock, the version check, the commutative comment merge and the section/evidence/collapse consumers behind one `_write_state` call (reckon/_store.py:1285), and the batch text write hides N ordered replacements behind one `replace_plan_text_batch` call (reckon/_store.py:1837); both interfaces are smaller than the behaviour they carry.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 leaves a second duplicate-id refusal live in `create_sprint` (reckon/mcp.py:2927) beside the shared owner `_refuse_duplicate_id (reckon/_store.py:2373)` it otherwise lands.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §10 adds a `replacements` parameter and a public `replace_plan_text_batch` without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design cites the machinery it extends by location (`_append_followup` reckon/mcp.py:2614, the sprint duplicate refusal reckon/mcp.py:2927, `_consistent_section_records` reckon/_schema.py, the setter in reckon/_store.py), and the per-file fence it lands generalises the pre-existing JSON-envelope flock (`_json_envelope_lock, now _serialized_path_lock, reckon/_store.py:274`) rather than adding a new lock.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §7 extends `append_to_list`'s existing refusal owner rather than adding a parallel check, §9 extends the existing `set section_declarations.<id>` path rather than adding an op, and §10's batch is a justified second input form on `replace_plan_text` (one lock, one version bump) rather than a wrapper: each states the change it makes to existing machinery.
